result: {"stdout":"# The chat's mind — target architecture (working doc, 2026-10-05)

Status: **proposal grounded in measurements.** Everything under "Measured" was run
against the live stack on 2026-10-05; everything else is design.

`the-fold` is a *surface*. It presents; it does not perceive, relate, or keep.
The triad it stands on (`khora/KHORA.md`, `FOLD-CONSTITUTION.md`):

| body | act | what it gives the chat |
|---|---|---|
| **khora** | perceive · produce ground | referents, addressed passages, grounding (`EORead@1`, `Ground@1`) |
| **janus** | relate · derive | what follows from the record: contradictions, equations, orderings — model-free |
| **penelope** | generate · keep · seal | the mouth, the artifact, the record, the facing page |

The chat's job: route a turn through those three, then **draw** what came back so a
person can see what stands on what. The model is the *mouth*: it phrases, orders,
translates; it never originates a fact (Constitution II.9) and never retrieves (IV.1).

## The turn, in six steps

1. **Classify** — smalltalk / creative / code / factual / follow-up. Creative, code and
   smalltalk carry *no claims*: no void note, no ✱, no sources (a poem has nothing to check).
2. **Perceive in context** — activation, not string search (`khora/native/docs/THE-HOLOGRAPH.md` §6):
   *a question activates its own referents, or the last answer's when it names none.* The
   chat keeps a per-chat referent record; "what happened to **him**" resolves to the last
   answer's referent **before** retrieval. Output: a *resolved question* shown to the person
   ("Read 'him' as Judge Richard Henderson"), never silently rewritten.
3. **Retrieve** — queries built from resolved referents, in the asker's script and, where
   different, the source language (Wikidata Q-ids link names across languages). Sources are
   read through the khora so passages carry addresses (byte ranges), not just snippets.
4. **Derive** — claims taken from the passages go to janus (`POST /api/reason` →
   `khora /v1/reason`): one-valued relations that two sources disagree on, equations
   (mathjs), orderings. Janus findings are *insights with premises*: each finding carries
   claim ids, each claim id carries its source span. Two grounds that disagree **are the
   finding** and are never averaged (III.4).
5. **Voice** — the mouth drafts from the material and the derived findings only, in the
   asker's language. Numbers, names, dates in the draft must resolve to a claim or a source
   span (II.9); anything else is typed `model` and drawn as such.
6. **Ground and draw** — every proposition gets a standing and links; the surface renders it.

## The proposition record (the one contract the surface renders)

input: {"stage":"READING / GRAMMAR PARSE: how khora turns text into structure (spans, rows, referents, UD parse, EOT, claim row) versus how the chat reads a retrieved web passage today, the router's web-down rule, and a grammar-aware proposal","summary":"Khora turns text into structure as a ladder, and "claim" is only the last rung. (1) Spans: adapters/text/spans.js splitSentences gives [{text, offset, order}] (vendored, pure). (2) Arrangement rows: relations-gfp.js extractGfpRelations gives {end1,label,end2,cell,grain,polarity,offset}; polarity is always "+", cell is grain_gap without a POS prior, and figures must recur (minRec 2) unless the caller INJECTS them. Legacy relations.js extractRelations gives {subject,verb,object,polarity,offset} from an injected verb set. (3) A UD parse: english-parser.js (16 MB perceptron model, English only, UPOS 95.2 / LAS 77.0 held out) then kernel/eot-rich.js toEot gives EOTRich@1 {surface, meaning:{nodes,markers,arcs}, gaps, span}; tense rides the cop marker. It is documented STANDALONE AND UNWIRED. (4) The perceiver recursive.js (referents by recurrence plus hyperedges), which is what /api/read serves through corpus-session.js. kernel/gfp-claim.js is not an extractor: it is the row {ground, rel, roles{ARG0,ARG1}, polarity, force, id, basis} with claimFromTriple as the single bridge; no "said" field exists anywhere. hyperlexicon, lexicon and ingestion are downstream ledgers; fact-block.js and source.js are vendored but need an injected reader (organs/hypergraph.js) that is not.

Measured by executing the pure modules (no model, no network). extractGfpRelations returns [] on a 2-sentence snippet; with only the question's referents injected it still returns [] on a real spider lead (connector 44 chars > MAX_LABEL 40) and a row only for "Spiders have eight legs." The SVO extractor, handed a verb list, returns spider/is/"an air-breathing arthropod that has eight legs" (relative clause swallowed) and, for World War II, "The war / ended / in 1945 ..." (anaphoric subject). The /v1/read code path gives 0 referents and 0 relations for 2 sentences; a 4-sentence lead gives 3 referents and one relation, missing the copular "is the king of the United Kingdom". The UD parser reads "Who is the king of the UK" correctly (root NOUN, cop, nmod PROPN) and tags every referent noun right in the spider and World War 2 asks, but mis-attaches the root in both do-support asks. Static closure analysis finds no node: import in recursive.js (29 files), relations-gfp (9), eot-rich (3), english-parser, gfp-claim, fact-gate, logos, reasoning-lint; ethos.js, solon.js, corpus-session.js and language-grammar.js have them.

The chat applies none of it to a web passage. Only engines, pathos, gary, flow and impression import vendor/khora; source, fact-block, grounding, cite, witness-sentences, run-dmca and corroboration are vendored with zero importers; client.read serves only coding tasks and attachments, and readingNote drops the participants the door returns. Web pages go DOMParser blocks, then Field-recall impressionOf (cue = every word of the ask), then raw text to the model or verbatim snips; ground.js is a lexical window verifier; attribution.js accepts "according to the sources" whenever anything was read (line 168).

Two reading failures reproduce purely. entitiesOf drops "UK" (length > 2), so "president of the UK" gates on "president", keeping US and France pages and rejecting Monarchy and PM of the UK. routeSources returns only web for spider and World War 2 (English cue regex), so upfront is empty and, with the relay at 502, webDown suppresses probe widening: zero sources.

Proposal: read the ask's grammar first. Frame = wh-phrase slot (what year, how many legs, who) plus remaining NOUN/PROPN/NUM chains as referents (spider; World War 2; king and UK). text:
The Popper baseline is done, and the triad design workflow is still running in the background.

**What I built**
- **Pre-registration:** [eval/falsify/PREREG.md](eval/falsify/PREREG.md). It states each conjecture as a universal that one counterexample refutes. Each is paired with a control the gate must let through, so "suppress everything" can't pass. I wrote predictions before running anything.
- **Driver:** [fold-e2e-popper.mjs](fold-e2e-popper.mjs) runs the real page with a forced-liar model, serves stubbed Wikipedia passages, and refuses every other search door. It reports `STANDS`, `FALSIFIED` or `UNMEASURED`, never "true".

**Baseline against today's build: 6 falsified, 6 stand (12 cases)**

| | result |
|---|---|
| C1 UK president | **Falsified.** The Queen Elizabeth II claim shipped under a footnote. |
| C2 king of the UK | **Falsified.** "Doesn't have a king" shipped while the passage says Charles III is king. |
| C3 king of France | **Falsified, and the worst.** "According to the sources, the king of France is Louis XVI" shipped as "1 passage from 1 source", with no flag at all. The passage says he was the last king (to 1792); word overlap was read as support. |
| C4 PM of the UK | **Falsified.** "Rishi Sunak" shipped; the passage says Andy Burnham. |
| C5 stopped ask | **Falsified.** The next turn's model input carried the stopped question (`system,user,user`). |
| C8 completeness | **Falsified.** Wikipedia was never asked for the basic question. |
| C6, K1, K2 | **Stand.** The "well?" fix holds, and both true answers still ship, so the baseline for over-withholding is clean. |
| K3 Eiffel unit conversion | **Stands, marked.** The model's own 1,082 ft shipped under the same footnote. |

**Where I was wrong**
- **C7:** I predicted it would fail. With the relay returning 502, the fold drew a typed gap instead of writing from memory. That's the intended behaviour.
- **K3 (first run):** it only "passed" because nothing was read. I fixed the harness and re-ran it.

**What the baseline says about the design:** the gate's only response to an unwitnessed sentence is a footnote. C2 and C3 are harder, because every word of the false sentence appears in the passage; only polarity and tense refute it, and word overlap can't see those. The logos leg has to read those two, and the design's plan will be judged on whether it makes C1–C5 and C8 survive while K1 and K2 keep standing.

I'll read the triad design when the workflow finishes, then run the implementation workflow against this same driver.

input: {"stage":"Seams, core and the full real-archon roster","summary":"TRIAD ON THE LIVE TURN. Only the pathos leg is live. The chat imports pathos.js (Abhinavagupta, with Murch's pacing.js and Panini's experiencer.js pulled in through its imports) plus the prompt door (Gary, Kondo, firewall) and Terry Gross (earned-cast.js). Solon/ethos.js and Logos/reasoning-lint.js are not vendored. ethos.js statically imports node:fs/path/url, and its dependencies privacy.js and askshape.js also read node:fs, so scripts/vendor-khora.mjs would skip it. logos.js (5-file closure) and reasoning-lint.js (4-file closure) have no node: imports and are vendorable. janus now hosts the same logos.js and reasoning-lint.js (the only difference is the gfp-claim import path). Neither missing leg addresses the six failures as built. Solon's clearance gates conduct (UDHR charter, privacy/PII), not provenance of facts. logos.js lints cycles and contradictions in a ledger, and none of failures 1-3 is a cycle or a contradiction among sources read.

THE REAL ROSTER IS NARROWER THAN THE CAST. The 16 ETHOS-ARCHONS figures (Ramakrishna, Vivekananda, Virgil, Pascal, Homer and the rest) are corpus-only: a manifest plus a header-only carrier with zero exports. Those carriers live in the-fold-latest, not in the current the-fold. Buddha has no manifest at all. The nine creativity-table archons are a name table and chorus-lint review lenses. Only Ostrom (provenance-cover.js) and Wilson (stigmergy.js) have organs. Diaconis, Holmes, Frankfurt, Dijkstra, Alexander, Feynman and Pearl are labels, and Marshall and Chekhov are lens names only. verification.js and creativity-table.js assign the interpretation row differently. The archon-holocracy "archons" are git-worktree missions, a separate naming system.

CORE AND SEAMS. Ashby is the code's "empty hub" (ashby.js:6). Ramakrishna is the corpus hub. Vivekananda's manifest points at experiencer.js, so the ethos-logos seam is carried by a file that sits in the pathos leg and is live via pathos.js. The compose() seam is explicitly archon-less (ethos-pipeline.mjs:340). The only code that makes ethos structurally precede logos is eo-teachings/composition.mjs, and it is not browser-safe (it imports ground-seal.mjs, which imports node:crypto).

WHERE THE FAILURES SIT. Gary's no-oracle-mode and the chat's NEVER_ALONE fire only when the material count is 0. The count is raw passages (fold-chat.js:1954), so irrelevant US and France articles count as material. checkAttributions accepts the generic "the sources" whenever any text of 40 characters or more was read, without testing the claim (fold-chat-attribution.js:168). # The Ethos Archons — the deep roles, and who sits where

*Design document, 2026-09-17. The cast of the ethos corpus (eo-teachings)
placed in the triad the reading kernel already organizes its organs by:
ethos (the ground), logos (the reasoning), pathos (the felt). This document
names the deep role each figure fills and the seam it occupies, so the
Handle-table roles, the archon-compendium entries, and the verified-quote
manifests all hang from one explicit map.*

## The triad, in this codebase's own words

- **ethos** — the GROUND. "The constitution producing a clearance the reader
  REQUIRES; ethos comes before logos" (organs/ethos.js, Solon). The gate.
- **logos** — the argument / the evidentiary walk. Is the claim coherent,
  productive, witnessed? The bulk of the kernel.
- **pathos** — the felt / the undergoing. "The felt shape of a reading, for
  whom" (organs/pathos.js, Abhinavagupta); the experiencer (Panini: "every
  belief carries who is undergoing it").

Seams between them are real positions, not blur — a figure who sits
*between* two legs governs the passage from one to the other.

## The deep roles

### RAMAKRISHNA — at the core (the experienced ground)

The core of the whole cast — not a leg but the hub the legs point at.
The Gospel of Sri Ramakrishna is the record of direct experience preceding
all doctrine: "God can be realized through all paths. All religions are
true" (the source's own witness of him). In THE-WAYS-OF-KNOWING.md he is
already the giver for PREDICTION (Friston, "disciplined by Ramakrishna")
and PROPRIOCEPTION (the sākṣin — "the knowing of oneself is not one more
object among the known"). He is the archon of the **realized core**: the
experience that grounds the ground, the hub that every path radiates from
and returns to. Deep role: **the core — the realized experience beneath
all doctrine; the hub of the wheel.**

### VIVEKANANDA — between ethos and logos

Took Ramakrishna's realization and gave it method — the four yogas (work,
worship, psychic control, philosophy) as the four ways the ground becomes a
walk. His Raja-Yoga opening is already the corpus manifest: "Each soul is
potentially divine. The goal is to manifest this Divinity within, by
controlling nature, external and internal. Do this either by work, or
worship, or psychic control, or philosophy." He is the archon of the
**will / discipline**: the one who carries the experienced ground (ethos)
into the methodical walk (logos) — the bridge where the gate becomes a
path. Deep role: **the four ways — the discipline that carries the ground
into the walk; the will between ethos and logos.**

### VIRGIL — between logos and pathos

The Aeneid's "fato profugus" — driven by fate through suffering — and, in
Dante, the guide through Hell and Purgatory who cannot enter Paradise.
Reason walking the reader through the felt underworld, stopping at the
threshold of the divine. He is the archon of the **guided passage**: logos
that walks beside pathos, that knows the way through the felt because it
has walked it, and that stops where reason must hand over. Deep role:
**the guide of the passage — reason walking the felt, stopping at the
threshold of the divine.**

### SHAKESPEARE — in pathos (the whole register)

Every character speaks true; the mirror held up to nature. The full
register of the experiencer — who undergoes, in every key, no flatness.
Deep role: **the whole register of the experiencer — who undergoes, in
every key.**

### DANTE — in pathos (the pilgrimage)

The pilgrim's arc through the three realms — the felt shape of the whole
journey, from the deepest descent to the highest ascent. Deep role: **the
pilgrim's arc — the felt shape of the whole passage, graded through its
three realms.**

### GEORGE ELIOT — in pathos (the unhistoric)

# Gate fix: pre-registration (frozen before any change to `fold-chat-ground.js`)

Frozen 2026-10-05, before the first code edit. Instrument: `eval/controls.mjs --live` (runs the working tree's own
`fold-chat-ground.js` against real Wikipedia text, no browser, no model). The only edits made to the instrument before
this freeze are the ones that ADD controls (a `--live` flag; classes SCRIPT, SCRIPTN, HOLDN, HOLDP). No existing control was
changed. Baseline = the unmodified gate, measured with that instrument (`eval/controls-baseline-live.json`).

## What is measured

| class | what | baseline (unmodified gate) |
|---|---|---|
| NEG single | 26 plainly false sentences, one article as material | 17/26 rejected |
| NEG pooled | the same 26, all 7 articles as material | 19/26 rejected |
| POS | 10 true near-verbatim | 9/10 accepted |
| DER | 12 true, not copied (units, paraphrase, markup, leaked `[W1]`) | 7/12 accepted |
| SELF | 7 verbatim same-language sentences (zh ja ru ar es fr de) | 7/7 accepted |
| SELFN | same, first number -> 7777 | 7/7 rejected |
| XLN | 4 false sentences in another language than the source | 4/4 rejected |
| XL | 12 true sentences in another language than the source | 1/12 accepted |
| SCRIPT (new) | 12 verbatim sentences, 4 each from hi / ar / zh Wikipedia (Hindi, Cairo, Beijing), split on that script's own terminator; 2 with digits + 2 without per script | 9/12 accepted (3 Hindi misses) |
| SCRIPTN (new) | the 6 digit-bearing ones with the first number -> 7777 | 6/6 rejected |
| HOLDN (new) | 12 held-out false English sentences written before the fix, NOT to be tuned against (3 are deliberately hard: h04 h07 h12) | 8/12 rejected |
| HOLDP (new) | 10 held-out true English sentences (verbatim fragments, 2 unit variants, 1 paraphrase) | 9/10 accepted |
| labels | `eval/labels.json`, 136 hand-labelled answer sentences, re-scored offline with the gate | strict precision 31/64 = 48.4%; recall 48/94 = 51.1% |

## Bars (no bar will be changed after this point; a miss is reported as a miss)

1. NEG: at least 24/26 rejected, single AND pooled.
2. The nine named false positives (n07 n08 n12 n14 n15 n20 n21 n22 n24) are all rejected, single AND pooled.
3. No regression: POS >= 9/10, SELF 7/7, SELFN 7/7, XLN 4/4, SCRIPTN 6/6, HOLDP >= 9/10.
4. DER (unit conversions and paraphrase) >= 10/12 accepted.
5. SCRIPT 12/12 accepted (verbatim hi / ar / zh must ground to the page they were copied from).
6. HOLDN (held-out) >= 10/12 rejected. (Baseline 8/12. The three deliberately hard ones may stay accepted; that is the stated limit of a lexical gate.)
7. Labels re-scored offline: strict precision rises above 48.4% AND recall stays >= 45%. The re-scorer must first
   reproduce the original app-flags on the unmodified gate (reported as agreement %, so the rig itself is checked).
   Any new citation whose quote differs from the old one is hand-read and labelled in `eval/labels-v2.json`, with a reason.
8. The two named mis-citations (labelled sentences "completed in 1889" cited to the 1887 petition page, and "capital of
   Australia is Canberra" cited to a quote that is only the question) must end up either ungrounded or cited to a quote that says it.
9. Cross-language is NOT faked: XL true sentences that cannot overlap lexically stay unaccepted unless the number+name
   evidence is real. Bar: of the XL sentences the gate does not accept, at least 11/12 carry the typed reason `cross-language`
   (a note, never a silent miss), and XLN stays 4/4 rejected.
10. `node --test` stays green (baseline 856 pass, 0 fail), with at least one test and one falsifier for every fix.

## Method guardrails

* Fixes are structural (same-window support, binding of numbers to their neighbours, tag/source stripping, unit table,
  Unicode tokenisation), never a word list built from the control sentences.

# The Fold — constitution

**The Fold is the whole system (naming, 2026-10-01).** The constitution governs
everything The Fold puts in front of a person, at every house and every surface
— the khora (the eoreader7 repo, the perceiver · ground-producer), penelope (the
keeper — the record · the mouth · the judgment), and the surfaces where the hand
comes back to the loom. The reading/research surface is **the fold** (the
holodeck repo, renamed). The former `the-fold` repo is being absorbed by plane
and will be archived; the laws below were written at the workbench they govern,
and they govern the whole.

The one governing document of the workbench. Everything the Fold puts in front
of a person — a cell, a view, a merge, a finding, an export — ships into one of
four **standings**, and this document decides which. `assay/` is its
enforcement: an artifact whose claim does not pass the articles does not render
as a finding.

`SEED-SPEAKER.md` says what the instrument is. A `LAWS.md` will say what went
wrong here. This says what may be produced, and under what standing.

**The mission is the invariant:** an earned, measured, faithful encounter with
data. Every article is in service of that. A ruling that weakens the encounter
is a misreading of this document, even where the letter of an article permits
it.

**The one operation is the physiology:** a finding is a difference against a
ground the workbench rebuilt by re-running the same computation on perturbed
input. Folding is a lossless change of resolution — the plain sentence and the
formal statement are one reading at two altitudes, never two claims — and from
every altitude there is a way back down to the rows.

**The two deaths are the failure modes:** *confabulation*, a rendered thing with
nothing beneath it; and *sclerosis*, a reader whose ground has closed, for whom
nothing on screen can any longer differ from what they already hold. Article II
governs the first. Article III governs the second, and is the half most
instruments omit.

**Articles cite their evidence.** Where an article rests on a measured result —
ours or the literature's — the appendix names it with its effect size. Where the
evidence is contested, the appendix says so rather than letting the article
borrow confidence it has not earned. An article resting on nothing but taste is
marked as such and may still be right.

---

## Article I — Standings

**I.1 `measured`.** Carries a ground, a descent, and a price: it re-ran on
licensed perturbed input, it drills to the rows, and the search that produced it
was counted. Only a `measured` artifact may be exported, cited, or called a
finding.

**I.2 `received`.** Given, never derived. What a column means, what counts as a
duplicate here, which rows are in scope, what the question is for. A prior is a
gift and **must name its giver**. Received knowledge is not weaker than measured
knowledge; it is knowledge of a different kind, and the only failure is its
being silently supplied rather than received.

**I.3 `shown`.** Raw output — anything a person ran that has not earned, or
cannot earn, a ground. Fully permitted, fully visible, permanently typed as what
it is. `shown` is where exploration lives and where most of a working session
should be.

**I.4 `refused`.** Not producible. The list is Articles II and III and it is
closed; anything not refused is permitted.

**I.5 The record is not a standing; it is the floor under all four.**
Append-only, holding what was run, against what, with what breadth, what it
eliminated, and what the reader predicted before seeing it. Deleting the
interface must change no computed result. Deleting the record retroactively
destroys every standing above it, and is therefore not an available operation.

---

Ask in this order. **Given? → Refused? → Grounded? → what remains is `shown`.**

result: {"stdout":"## Article IV — The seams

**IV.1 Derive vs receive.** A model reranks and phrases what the workbench
surfaced; it never retrieves on its own. Where the workbench surfaced nothing,
it returns a typed gap, never a memory.

**IV.2 Pure vs host.** Seed, clock, entropy, and I/O come from the host — which
is what makes any computation re-runnable as its own null (II.4).

**IV.3 A missing prior is a typed gap, never a silently wrong number.** Six
kinds of silence, no two rendering alike: not-present, not-computed,
computed-and-empty, refused-as-underpowered, censored-above (surfeit — the
trigger to re-zero), censored-below (regularity, not to be mistaken for it).
**Downstream computation may not derive through a gap** — it inherits it.

**IV.4 `shown` is typed, never blocked.** People must be able to look at raw
output, try things, and follow hunches; a workbench that refuses to display what
it cannot certify is one people will leave, and leaving is the worst outcome
available. The invariant is not that everything is grounded. It is that
`measured` and `shown` never render alike.

**IV.5 The register is the reader's.** Nobody is assigned an altitude by an
inference about their competence, and no register is more confident than the one
below it. Where the formal register refuses a number, the plain register refuses
it in fewer words.

---

## Article V — The claim, and its verdicts
-----
## Article VII — What is deliberately not refused

Bad questions, ugly charts, doomed hypotheses, unfashionable methods, work done
in the wrong order, and analyses this instrument's authors would consider
misguided are permitted and always will be. So is any computation whatever: no
method is on an approved list, because a rule admitting only blessed statistics
is the one-off fix the convergence test refuses, and because every obligation in
Article II attaches to the *result*, never to the technique.

**The constitution refuses claims, not curiosity.** Everything above governs
what may be asserted, exported, or handed to another person under the standing
`measured`. None of it governs what may be tried.

---

-----
# The Ethos Archons — the deep roles, and who sits where

ethos (the ground), logos (the reasoning), pathos (the felt). This document
names the deep role each figure fills and the seam it occupies, so the
Handle-table roles, the archon-compendium entries, and the verified-quote
manifests all hang from one explicit map.*

*between* two legs governs the passage from one to the other.

**Find, snip, cite — never rewrite.** The Fold finds a source, shows the source's OWN words (verbatim snip) under the creator's name with a link back, and does not paraphrase or retype content (recipes especially). Most asks need no model-written text at all.

**Two answer modes (user, 2026-10-05):** (1) *Facing page* — a model response drawn from snipped sources, shown beside them; (2) *Sources only* — the sources' verbatim snips strung together with citations, NO model call. **Never is it just the model talking:** a turn with no sources yields only an app-authored typed gap, never a model answer. Open question I raised: creative / code / transform / compute / smalltalk asks have no sources — interim behaviour is app-authored cards/notes behind a single `ALONE_KINDS` constant until the user decides.

**Tipping creators:** when content comes from a creator, offer to "tip the source" and say plainly it is a feature in development (the card's tip button only shows an 'in development, nothing sent' toast). The user then asked for an email-finder + `mailto:` outreach feature (find the author's contact on the page, "going to the IP owner if needed"). The auto-mode classifier blocked the first step as a real-world transaction; I did NOT build it and did not route around the block. If the user wants it: it must be user-initiated mailto only (nothing sent by the app), use only contacts the page itself publishes (never guess addresses, never use hosting-provider abuse contacts), and say where each address was found.

**n8n relay (`n8n.intelechia.com/webhook/feed`) is for TESTING only — never wire it into the app.** Measured as a search egress it was excellent (Brave page parsed 20/20, DDG 19/20) but the workflow has an SSRF hole (it fetched the n8n host's own `127.0.0.1:5678/healthz`); tell the user to add a private-address guard/allowlist/secret before anyone relies on it.

**Don't paste long copyrighted source text in replies**: describe snips by source/id; the app card shows them, my messages don't.

See [[chat-focus-and-search]], [[the-fold-naming]].

Added and run: the baseline now has two cases for "the search must falsify its answers", and both are falsified.

- **C9:** the search stage runs exactly one query per turn, the ask itself ("Who is the monarch of the UK?"). In the stub world, the page that refutes Queen Elizabeth II is reachable only by a query that names her. The fold never issues that query, so the refutation can't be found.
- **C10:** the draft ships under the same footnote, and no refuting passage appears on screen.

I wrote both into [eval/falsify/PREREG.md](eval/falsify/PREREG.md) as Amendment 1, with predictions made before running. In the driver ([fold-e2e-popper.mjs](fold-e2e-popper.mjs)), the stub's refuting page is only reachable if the fold chooses to make that query; the harness never hands it over.

**The design workflow:** it has already finished its synthesis step, so it won't contain this. When it completes, I'll run a revision pass with "the search is the falsifier" as a hard constraint. For each candidate claim it must issue a query built to break it (the claim itself, other holders, later dates). A claim ships only as "searched here for a counterexample, found none". If a refutation turns up, it is drawn next to the claim, not footnoted.

Your message ended at "what". If you meant a question or something I've misread, tell me and I'll adjust.

result: {"stdout":" * missing member skips that machinery entirely rather than degrading
 * through it). Closing the class is the P43-sanctioned move ("a received
 * class that closes a false binding is turned on, not left opt-in") —
 * every added form is a standard, closed, enumerable English orthographic
 * contraction, same giver, not a hand-picked or open-ended addition.
 */
export const NEGATION_WORDS = Object.freeze(new Set([
  "not", "never", "hardly", "scarcely", "neither", "nor",
  "didn't", "don't", "doesn't", "wouldn't", "couldn't", "shouldn't",
  "won't", "can't", "cannot",
  "isn't", "aren't", "wasn't", "weren't",
  "haven't", "hasn't", "hadn't",
  "mustn't", "needn't", "shan't", "daren't", "mightn't", "oughtn't",
]));
export const NEGATION_WORDS_META = Object.freeze({ giver: "lang/en", scope: null });

/**
 * Negation correlatives — the closed set of adverbs that, immediately after
 * a standalone "not", turn it from a negator into an affirmative correlative
 * conjunction: "not only X but also Y", "not just X but also Y" both assert
 * BOTH X and Y, never a negation of either. Found live (2026-09-23): the
 * relation extractor's own negation scan read "not" in "This decentralization
 * not only provides users with more control... but also enhances..." as
 * negating the clause it introduces, when the construction is affirmative.
 * "not just ..., but also ..." is independently named in this repo's own
 * CODING-LESSONS.md:1348 as a pair that must never be split, confirming the
 * class is a real, recurring English construction, not a specimen of one.
 * Scoped to the standalone "not" alternative only (relations.js's
 * negationBeforeVerbFor) — "never only"/"cannot only" etc. have no such
 * correlative reading and are unaffected.
 */
 * "how" and "why" are deliberately NOT here — they ask after a manner or a
 * reason, which is an explanation and not a filler, so they carry no head
 * noun to gloss. They are their own class, MANNER_REASON_PRONOUNS below,
 * because the distinction is what lets a caller refuse a slot outright
 * rather than opening one it can never fill.
 */
export const INTERROGATIVE_PRONOUNS = Object.freeze(new Map([
  ["who", "person"],
  ["whom", "person"],
  ["whose", "person"],
  ["what", "thing"],
  ["which", "thing"],
  ["where", "place"],
  ["when", "time"],
]));
export const INTERROGATIVE_PRONOUNS_META = Object.freeze({ giver: "lang/en", scope: null });

/**
 * The two interrogatives that ask after a manner or a reason rather than
 * after a filler. Split from INTERROGATIVE_PRONOUNS above on the grammar's
 * own line, not on a caller's convenience: "who was X" names a slot some
 * entity occupies, "why was X" names no slot at all, and a reader that
 * cannot tell those apart will open an answer slot for a question that has
 * none and then report it unfilled forever.
 */
export const MANNER_REASON_PRONOUNS = Object.freeze(new Set(["how", "why"]));

result: {"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/Users/mlacy/Documents/3.0/the-fold/vendor/khora/native/adapters/text/priors.js","content":"/**
 * Interrogative pro-forms, each mapped to the KIND OF THING it asks for.
 *
 * A closed grammatical class in the same standing as ANAPHORIC_PRONOUNS
 * below: English has these and no others, and the gloss on each is the
 * lexicographic fact any dictionary states for the word ("who" asks after a
 * person) — NOT an ontology this engine invented and not a type system. The
 * value is the head noun a reader would supply if asked to finish "this
 * question is asking for a ___", nothing more.
 *
 * A Map rather than a Set because the gloss IS the received content: a
 * caller that only needs membership can still ask `.has`, but a caller that
 * drops the gloss and keeps the keys has thrown away the half of this prior
 * that was worth receiving.
 *
 * "how" and "why" are deliberately NOT here — they ask after a manner or a
 * reason, which is an explanation and not a filler, so they carry no head
 * noun to gloss. They are their own class, MANNER_REASON_PRONOUNS below,
 * because the distinction is what lets a caller refuse a slot outright
 * rather than opening one it can never fill.
 */
export const INTERROGATIVE_PRONOUNS = Object.freeze(new Map([
  ["who", "person"],
  ["whom", "person"],
  ["whose", "person"],
  ["what", "thing"],
  ["which", "thing"],
  ["where", "place"],
  ["when", "time"],
]));
export const INTERROGATIVE_PRONOUNS_META = Object.freeze({ giver: "lang/en", scope: null });

/**
 * The two interrogatives that ask after a manner or a reason rather than
 * after a filler. Split from INTERROGATIVE_PRONOUNS above on the grammar's
 * own line, not on a caller's convenience: "who was X" names a slot some
 * entity occupies, "why was X" names no slot at all, and a reader that
 * cannot tell those apart will open an answer slot for a question that has
 * none and then report it unfilled forever.
 */
export const MANNER_REASON_PRONOUNS = Object.freeze(new Set(["how", "why"]));
export const MANNER_REASON_PRONOUNS_META = Object.freeze({ giver: "lang/en", scope: null });

export const ANAPHORIC_PRONOUNS = Object.freeze(new Set([
  "it", "it's", "this", "this's", "that", "that's", "these", "those",
]));
export const ANAPHORIC_PRONOUNS_META = Object.freeze({ giver: "lang/en", scope: null });

/**
 * Possessive determiners — a closed grammatical class, distinct from
 * DEFINITE_DETERMINERS above (a possessive presupposes a possessor, a
 * definite article presupposes only identifiability) and distinct from
 * ANAPHORIC_PRONOUNS (a possessive determiner always precedes a noun; an
 * anaphoric pronoun optionally stands alone). Both facts a consumer reads
 * from context, never from this set alone.
 */
export const POSSESSIVE_DETERMINERS = Object.freeze(new Set([
  "my", "your", "his", "her", "its", "our", "their",
]));
export const POSSESSIVE_DETERMINERS_META = Object.freeze({ giver: "lang/en", scope: null });

/**
 * Coordinating conjunctions that join two noun phrases into one (as
 * opposed to joining two independent clauses, which every member of this
 * set can also do — a consumer distinguishing the two reads what stands on
 * each side, not this set alone). Scoped to "and"/"or" deliberately: they
 * are the unambiguous NP-coordinators; "but"/"nor"/"yet"/"so" more often
 * join clauses than phrases in ordinary prose and are left OUT rather than
 * risked — a narrower true set, not a wider guessed one.
 */","numLines":70,"startLine":150,"totalLines":417}}

I opened /Users/mlacy/Documents/3.0/the-fold/fold-chat-channels.js:236-248. modelHistory(messages) loops with `if (!m || m.role === "system") continue;` (line 239). Then `const content = modelText(m); if (m.role === "assistant" && !content.trim()) continue;` (line 241). A sources-authored assistant turn is pushed as `{ role, content: SOURCES_NOTE + content }` (line 244). Every other turn, user turns included, goes through `out.push({ role: m.role, content })` (line 245). I found nothing in the function that drops, flags or filters an unanswered user ask.

The failure-6 chain checks out end to end:
1. fold-chat.js:1787-1790, the `stopped` handler, pushes `{ role: "assistant", content: "", ..., notices }`. The user's ask stays in s.messages, and the stopped note is carried in message.notices.
2. modelHistory drops that empty assistant turn (line 241) and keeps the user ask before it (line 245).
3. fold-chat.js:1763 builds `const history = modelHistory(s.messages)`, and line 1957 passes `history: history.slice(0, -1)` to garyDoor.composeTurn. slice(0,-1) removes only the current ask, so the earlier unanswered ask stays in the model's context.
4. buildTurnMessages in vendor/the-fold/fold.js:479-499 pushes each history entry as-is with `messages.push({ role: m.role, content: m.content })` (lines 496-497), then the question last. It does no filtering either.
5. fold-chat-thread.js `unansweredAsk` (line 112) handles only the "well?" retry search path, not the model history. It does not strip the stopped ask from history.

So the model does see a stopped, unanswered ask next to the new question. That is the mechanism behind failure 6.

Two literal inaccuracies in the claim:
- "skips only empty assistant turns" is false. Line 239 also skips null entries and every `role === "system"` message.
- "pushes every other turn" misses that a sources-authored assistant turn (m.authored === "sources") is pushed with the SOURCES_NOTE prefix, `"[Passages quoted from sources — not written by you:] "` (defined at fold-chat-channels.js:28, used at line 244). Neither point affects failure 6.","correction":"Corrected wording: modelHistory (fold-chat-channels.js:236-248) skips null entries and `role: "system"` messages (line 239) and skips assistant turns whose modelText is empty (line 241). It pushes user turns as written (line 245). It pushes sources-authored assistant turns with the SOURCES_NOTE prefix (line 244). Because a stopped turn stores an empty assistant message (fold-chat.js:1790) and the user's ask stays, modelHistory has no filter that removes the unanswered ask. fold-chat.js:1957 passes history.slice(0,-1) to the model, so a stopped ask rides into the next turn's context (failure 6). Fixing it would need the history builder, or the caller, to drop a user ask that has no answer after it (inferred as a fix; not present in the code today)."}

input: {"refuted":false,"evidence":"I opened /Users/mlacy/Documents/3.0/khora/native/adapters/text/grammar.js in full (91 lines) and ran a read-only node import of it. The claim holds on all its main points.

- Header and purpose (lines 1-34): "THE GRAMMAR REGISTER". The header says a language with no registered grammar "returns `no_grammar_for_language`" and "Never an English attempt on Russian material".
- HOLON_LEVELS (line 42) is frozen ["name","phrase","clause","sentence","paragraph","section","document"], matching the claimed order. The node import printed the same array.
- grammarFor (lines 61-66): the key is the lowercased first segment of the language code. An unregistered language returns { gap: { reason: "no_grammar_for_language", language, registered, detail } }. Running grammarFor('ru') returned exactly that gap, with registered ["en"]. The only registered grammar is en (GRAMMARS, lines 48-58).
- grammarAt (lines 69-75) returns a typed gap for an unknown level or for no_grammar_at_level. levelOfHolon (lines 78-88) maps the last address segment to a level. Running it gave '/' -> document, '/p1/s2' -> sentence, '/p1/s2/c3' -> clause, '/x' -> null. registeredLanguages (line 90) returned ["en"].
- Imports (lines 35-40): priors.js, name-spans.js, clause-spans.js, spans.js, phasepost.js and occupancy-testimony.js, six in all. The module loaded without error under node, so every named import resolves.

Closure check, which the claim left unverified. A grep of the six imported files, plus kernel/undecided.js (imported at occupancy-testimony.js:66), found no node: imports, require(, readFileSync or process. usage. The only import lines in those files are the relative ones already named, plus occupancy-testimony.js:66 and 433. priors.js and phasepost.js have no imports. So the closure appears node-free by grep (inferred, not browser-tested).

Gaps in the claim as written:
1. The export list is incomplete. grammar.js also exports PREPOSITIONS_EN (line 45) and PREPOSITIONS_EN_META (line 46). The node import printed 7 keys: HOLON_LEVELS, PREPOSITIONS_EN, PREPOSITIONS_EN_META, grammarAt, grammarFor, levelOfHolon, registeredLanguages.
2. grammarFor has a second typed gap. With no language declared (empty, undefined), line 63 returns reason "no_language_declared", not no_grammar_for_language.
3. A prototype-key leak, which I observed by running it. Line 64 does `GRAMMARS[key]` and line 65 does `g ?? gap`, and GRAMMARS is a plain frozen object. grammarFor('constructor') therefore returned a function (the Object constructor), not a gap. grammarAt('constructor', level) would then throw a TypeError at line 73. grammarFor('toString') returned a gap only because the key is lowercased to 'tostring'. This is an edge case, since no real language code is "constructor". It does mean "returns the grammar or a typed gap" is not strictly total.","correction":"Restate the claim as follows.

grammar.js exports HOLON_LEVELS, PREPOSITIONS_EN, PREPOSITIONS_EN_META, grammarFor, grammarAt, levelOfHolon and registeredLanguages.

grammarFor(language) returns the registered grammar. Only 'en' is registered, at line 48. Otherwise it returns a typed gap: no_language_declared (line 63) when no language is declared, or no_grammar_for_language (line 65) when the language is unregistered.

Edge case: grammarFor('constructor') returns the Object function instead of a gap, because lines 64-65 index a plain object with `??`. Fixing that needs a Map or Object.hasOwn.

The import closure was checked by grep only and is node-free. A real browser import of grammar.js is still unconfirmed."}

**Why:** the standalone bridge (heimdall up, :8790) was the failure point — unsupervised, stale code, a browser tab as the only fleet controller, and its floor depended on khora's proxy (11434) which it did not own. Measured diagnosis in [[the-fold-pipeline-findings]] style: no timeout/abort/step-down on rung 4, frontier map cleared on a failed probe, no circuit breaker, /bridge/* unauthenticated.

**How to apply:**
- Each server (khora channel, penelope mouth, the Fold's server) mounts heimdall in-process (`createBridge` handler, no process.exit/pidfile/global state); each instance's floor (own Ollama, in-tab) works with zero peers = "possibility". Peer coordination, fleet horses, native links, frontier = "probability" layers above it.
- Low layers = possibility (always exist), high layers = probability (make the good path usual). A broken higher rung steps down; the record shows the drop.
- `heimdall/scripts/floor.sh` supervises via launchd; the bridge service there is marked `transitional` until embedding lands.
- Approved by operator the same day: restart live bridge after fixes land, launchd install, node-datachannel install, per-boot token + Host check on the gate.

name: heimdall-embedded-peers
description: Heimdall is not a standalone daemon — every server embeds its own heimdall and the instances coordinate as peers (decided 2026-10-05)
metadata:
  node_type: memory

Operator decision 2026-10-05: "every server has a heimdall, and they coordinate, but there is no standalone heimdall."

**Why:** the standalone bridge (heimdall up, :8790) was the failure point — unsupervised, stale code, a browser tab as the only fleet controller, and its floor depended on khora's proxy (11434) which it did not own. Measured diagnosis in [[the-fold-pipeline-findings]] style: no timeout/abort/step-down on rung 4, frontier map cleared on a failed probe, no circuit breaker, /bridge/* unauthenticated.

**How to apply:**
- Each server (khora channel, penelope mouth, the Fold's server) mounts heimdall in-process (`createBridge` handler, no process.exit/pidfile/global state); each instance's floor (own Ollama, in-tab) works with zero peers = "possibility". Peer coordination, fleet horses, native links, frontier = "probability" layers above it.
- Low layers = possibility (always exist), high layers = probability (make the good path usual). A broken higher rung steps down; the record shows the drop.
- `heimdall/scripts/floor.sh` supervises via launchd; the bridge service there is marked `transitional` until embedding lands.
- Approved by operator the same day: restart live bridge after fixes land, launchd install, node-datachannel install, per-boot token + Host check on the gate.

**Progress 2026-10-05 (rebuild, nothing committed yet — 78 files changed in heimdall/):**
- Done + verified (483 tests green): floor (timeouts, abort, upstream step-down list, /v1/messages translation), frontier (429/5xx throw, map not cleared on empty probe, circuit breaker, rung-failed ledger), gate (Host check, per-boot token ~/.heimdall/bridge.token, body cap, XSS, traversal), fleet controller defects (liveness/lease/revocation/relink), src/peers.js + peers-http.js (39 tests, NOT yet wired into any server), scripts/floor.sh (launchd; plists installed in ~/Library/LaunchAgents, only com.fold.bridge loaded).
- Live: bridge runs under launchd (8790, ~27s boot). channel (khora 11434) and mouth (penelope 11439) are still hand-started — cut over with `floor.sh adopt` only when no eval is running (evals were using them). ~/.heimdall/floor.env (0600) holds OPENCODE_SERVER_* + HEIMDALL_ALLOWED_ORIGINS.
- NOT done: embed heimdall (createBridge handler + peers handler + peers.tick) into khora proxy / penelope mouth / the Fold's server; headless controller src/controller.js (node-datachannel install approved); Fold key-entry needs token cookie or `heimdall key`; commit the untracked modules together (audit, competence, job-lane, route-stats, websearch, keycheck, key-cli, floor, bridge-testkit, vertex, acceptance, escalation, peers*, controller-core).
- Another session owns the Vertex DeepSeek lane edits (vertex.js + one-line hooks, and the 403 on /api/providers/keys for vertex) — keep them.

input: {"refuted":false,"evidence":"I could not refute the core claim. I opened /Users/mlacy/Documents/3.0/khora/native/adapters/text/grammar.js in full (91 lines) and ran node against it.

- **Register and Chomsky:** The header (lines 1-2) reads "THE GRAMMAR REGISTER (2026-09-28)". Chomsky appears only in the quoted user direction on line 4 ("Be sure this, Chomsky, is properly connected..."). That matches the archon definition in /Users/mlacy/Documents/3.0/khora/native/organs/archon-compendium.js:492-498, name "Noam Chomsky" (credit line: "a role grammar is declared, never the default").
- **grammarFor gap:** Lines 61-66 read `const g = GRAMMARS[key]; return g ?? { gap: { reason: "no_grammar_for_language", language: key, registered: Object.keys(GRAMMARS), detail: ...refuses, never attempts another language's } }`. Node run: fr and ru return `no_grammar_for_language`. en and en-GB return en.
- **Exports:** The five named exports exist: `HOLON_LEVELS` (line 42, frozen, name,phrase,clause,sentence,paragraph,section,document), `grammarFor` (61), `grammarAt` (69), `levelOfHolon` (78), `registeredLanguages` (90). The node run printed the full export list: HOLON_LEVELS, PREPOSITIONS_EN, PREPOSITIONS_EN_META, grammarAt, grammarFor, levelOfHolon, registeredLanguages.
- **Imports:** Lines 35-40 import from priors.js, name-spans.js, clause-spans.js, spans.js, phasepost.js and occupancy-testimony.js. I grepped each source file and confirmed every imported symbol is exported there: nameSpans, nameNesting, NAME_PARTICLES, clauseSpans, splitSentences, COPULA_FORMS, LOCATIVE_PREPOSITIONS and OCCUPANCY_TRANSITIONS_EN, among others.
- **Node-free closure (the part the claim left unverified):** I grepped priors.js, name-spans.js, clause-spans.js, spans.js, phasepost.js, occupancy-testimony.js and kernel/undecided.js for `node:`, `require(`, `import(`, `process.` and fs imports. There were no hits. The only transitive imports are the priors.js imports in clause-spans.js:87, spans.js:235 and name-spans.js:71, plus occupancy-testimony.js:66-67 and 433 (kernel/undecided.js, priors.js, name-spans.js). priors.js, phasepost.js and kernel/undecided.js have no imports (kernel/undecided.js by grep, not read in full). Static closure is therefore node-free; I did not run it in a browser.","correction":"The claim holds, but it is incomplete or slightly loose in four places:
1. The export list is not exhaustive. grammar.js also exports `PREPOSITIONS_EN` (line 45) and `PREPOSITIONS_EN_META` (line 46), seven exports in all.
2. grammarFor can return a gap other than `no_grammar_for_language`: `no_language_declared` for empty, null or undefined input (line 63). grammarAt adds `unknown_level` (line 70) and `no_grammar_at_level` (line 74).
3. "Returns the grammar or a typed gap" is not strictly true. The lookup `GRAMMARS[key]` (line 64) has no own-property check, so `grammarFor("constructor")` returns the `Object` function, not a gap (node run: `"constructor" => FUNCTION Object`). The fallback `g ?? gap` never fires there. It is not an English attempt on another language, and no real language code collides, but it breaks the gap-or-grammar contract.
4. Only "en" is registered (`registeredLanguages()` returned `['en']`). Normalisation only splits on `-` or `_`, so ISO 639-3 "eng" returns `no_grammar_for_language`. That is a gap, not an English attempt, but it is a limitation.

The Chomsky label comes from the user-direction comment on line 4 plus the archon-compendium entry. Nothing in grammar.js's own code names Chomsky."}

User statement (2026-10-05): "every server has a heimdall, and they coordinate, but there is not standalone heimdall." Benchmarks and tools must drive models THROUGH the running heimdalls (sealed gate, audit ledger), never call providers directly, and must discover heimdalls rather than assume one. Ports seen: 8790 = the real `heimdall up` (served local models only, no free lanes), 8795/8796 = other sessions' bridges that list pollinations + llm7.

User direction: WebLLM is the default engine for heimdall (a request naming no model rides a ready browser WebLLM worker; named models are never redirected), and WebLLM must install/run only once per browser (one engine per browser via navigator.locks + BroadcastChannel; weights already shared via Cache Storage). Built in heimdall `src/engine-share.js` (SharedEngine, wired in main.js) and `defaultToWebllm` in bridge-server.mjs; tests engine-share/bridge-webllm-default.

Free-model benchmark: heimdall `scripts/free-bench.mjs` + `src/free-bench.js` (families: sealed-capsule "order" with symbol-only follow-ups, and masked-placeholder "mask" code edit). Results in `heimdall/docs/data/free-bench/`. Scheduled task `heimdall-free-bench` runs `--quick` every 6 h (user asked for periodic runs once it worked). First run: everything DOWN (Pollinations 500/timeout, LLM7 daily-quota 429, Ollama busy).

**Why:** the user wants free models measured for active / fast / accurate, and the architecture is a coordinated set of heimdalls.

**How to apply:** route through heimdall; keep paid lanes (e.g. the owner-only `vertex` lane) out of free comparisons. Known unfixed bug: remote.js (~lines 48/108/189) returns a provider 429 as an empty result, so the bridge answers HTTP 200 with empty text; callers cannot tell quota from silence. remote.js/bridge-server.mjs had other sessions' uncommitted edits. # Embedding heimdall in a host server (`src/embed.js`)

There is no standalone heimdall. khora's proxy, penelope's mouth and the Fold's server each mount their own, in-process,
and the instances coordinate as peers (docs/PEERS.md). Each floor works with ZERO peers (possibility); peers only add options.

## The hook (put it FIRST in the host's request handler, before its default-deny)

    import { mountHeimdall } from "../heimdall/src/embed.js";                       // 1
    const hm = mountHeimdall({ name: "penelope-mouth", selfUrl: `http://127.0.0.1:${port}/heimdall/peers`, peerUrls: [KHORA_URL + "/heimdall/peers"] }); // 2
    http.createServer(async (req, res) => {                                          // 3
      if (await hm.handle(req, res)) return;                                         // 4  true = it was /heimdall/*, answered
      /* ...the host's own routes and its 404... */ });  server.on("close", () => hm.close()); // 5

`handle` never throws, never listens, and for a path outside `/heimdall` is a synchronous prefix check (an already-resolved
`false`; no I/O, no timer). An internal error is a 500 JSON for `/heimdall/*` only. The host owns the port.

## Routes under `/heimdall`

The bridge's doors (`/api/chat`, `/api/generate`, `/v1/*`, `/api/job`, `/link/*` ...), `/peers/*` (peer wire, shared token),
`GET /status` = `{schema:"HeimdallEmbed@1", name, floors:[{url,up}], peers, stats, token:false, startedAt}` (the token is never
sent; the bridge's own status moved to `/bridge-status`). Loopback Host wall and the bridge's token rule are the bridge's own.

## Options (`mountHeimdall(opts)` -> `{ handle, status, peers, bridge, close, refresh }`)

- `name` (required, unique per server). `prefix` (default `/heimdall`; every host in a peer set must use the same one).
- `floors` ordered upstream URLs; default `[]` = `OLLAMA_HOST`, else `http://127.0.0.1:11435`. Never point a floor at a heimdall.
- `peerUrls` static peers (`http://127.0.0.1:PORT/heimdall/peers`); `selfUrl` is what you tell them (needed so they recognise you).
  `trustPeers` (default true: the list is the operator's allowlist for `local-raw` jobs); `privacy` (default `local-raw`); `allowHosts`.
- `stateDir` (default `~/.heimdall/<name>/`): `bridge.token` 0600, `peers.json`, links, state, ledger, competence; nothing else is written.
  The peer token is SHARED by same-machine peers: `~/.heimdall/peers.token` (0600) by default, or `<stateDir>/peers.token` when you inject
  `stateDir`; to peer with an injected `stateDir` also pass `peerTokenFile`/`peerToken`. `homeDir` moves the default root.
- `bridgeOptions` passed to `createBridge` (e.g. `allowedOrigins`, `upstreamFirstByteMs`). `localQueueMs` (default 10000).
  `peerOptions` -> `createPeerSet` (`firstByteMs` 8000, `lendBelow` 2 ...). `autoTick` (default true: `refresh()` every `tickMs`=15 s
  on an unref'd timer: look at the floors, advertise their models, hello the peers, `setLoad` from live inflight).
  Injectable: `clock`, `timers`, `fetch`, `fs`, `env`, `log` (the only output; none by default).

## The ladder rule (POST `/heimdall/api/chat`, `/heimdall/api/generate`)

0. No peer known at all: straight to the plain bridge, unchanged. A peer that never said hello (not `ready`) is not eligible and costs 0.
1. **Peers first ONLY** when the floors answered, none holds the model, no fleet tab serves it, AND an eligible peer holds it.
2. Otherwise the **local floor runs first**; if it answers (any head not in 404/429/500/502/503/504/508), that is the answer. A peer is never asked.
3. If its head is one of those refusals, BEFORE any body byte: one peer attempt (`peers.run`, bounded by `firstByteMs`). No peer, or it
   fails: the local refusal is replayed as the plain bridge would have sent it. A dead peer therefore adds at most `firstByteMs` once, then its break… [652 more chars at the transcript address]

result: {"stdout":"# The Ethos Archons — the deep roles, and who sits where

*Design document, 2026-09-17. The cast of the ethos corpus (eo-teachings)
placed in the triad the reading kernel already organizes its organs by:
ethos (the ground), logos (the reasoning), pathos (the felt). This document
names the deep role each figure fills and the seam it occupies, so the
Handle-table roles, the archon-compendium entries, and the verified-quote
manifests all hang from one explicit map.*

## The triad, in this codebase's own words

- **ethos** — the GROUND. "The constitution producing a clearance the reader
  REQUIRES; ethos comes before logos" (organs/ethos.js, Solon). The gate.
- **logos** — the argument / the evidentiary walk. Is the claim coherent,
  productive, witnessed? The bulk of the kernel.
- **pathos** — the felt / the undergoing. "The felt shape of a reading, for
  whom" (organs/pathos.js, Abhinavagupta); the experiencer (Panini: "every
  belief carries who is undergoing it").

Seams between them are real positions, not blur — a figure who sits
*between* two legs governs the passage from one to the other.

## The deep roles

### RAMAKRISHNA — at the core (the experienced ground)

The core of the whole cast — not a leg but the hub the legs point at.
The Gospel of Sri Ramakrishna is the record of direct experience preceding
all doctrine: "God can be realized through all paths. All religions are
true" (the source's own witness of him). In THE-WAYS-OF-KNOWING.md he is
already the giver for PREDICTION (Friston, "disciplined by Ramakrishna")
and PROPRIOCEPTION (the sākṣin — "the knowing of oneself is not one more
object among the known"). He is the archon of the **realized core**: the
experience that grounds the ground, the hub that every path radiates from
and returns to. Deep role: **the core — the realized experience beneath
all doctrine; the hub of the wheel.**

### VIVEKANANDA — between ethos and logos

Took Ramakrishna's realization and gave it method — the four yogas (work,
worship, psychic control, philosophy) as the four ways the ground becomes a
walk. His Raja-Yoga opening is already the corpus manifest: "Each soul is
potentially divine. The goal is to manifest this Divinity within, by
controlling nature, external and internal. Do this either by work, or
worship, or psychic control, or philosophy." He is the archon of the
**will / discipline**: the one who carries the experienced ground (ethos)
into the methodical walk (logos) — the bridge where the gate becomes a
path. Deep role: **the four ways — the discipline that carries the ground
into the walk; the will between ethos and logos.**

### VIRGIL — between logos and pathos

The Aeneid's "fato profugus" — driven by fate through suffering — and, in
Dante, the guide through Hell and Purgatory who cannot enter Paradise.
Reason walking the reader through the felt underworld, stopping at the
threshold of the divine. He is the archon of the **guided passage**: logos
that walks beside pathos, that knows the way through the felt because it
has walked it, and that stops where reason must hand over. Deep role:
**the guide of the passage — reason walking the felt, stopping at the
threshold of the divine.**

### SHAKESPEARE — in pathos (the whole register)

Every character speaks true; the mirror held up to nature. The full
register of the experiencer — who undergoes, in every key, no flatness.
Deep role: **the whole register of the experiencer — who undergoes, in
every key.**

### DANTE — in pathos (the pilgrimage)

The pilgrim's arc through the three realms — the felt shape of the whole
journey, from the deepest descent to the highest ascent. Deep role: **the
pilgrim's arc — the felt shape of the whole passage, graded through its
three realms.**

(`acceptDuty` interval), and the lease is 12 h by the worker's own hand.

The chat's gate is `fold-chat-ground.js`, a lean fork of the khora's `organs/cite.js` + `organs/grounding.js`. The fix
for the defects in `docs/GATE-FIX-PREREG.md` was made and measured HERE. `vendor/khora/` is a frozen copy
(`VENDOR-KHORA.json`: "Never edit by hand") and `/Users/mlacy/Documents/3.0/khora` was not touched. This file is the
exact change each of those defects asks of the khora, in the order of the khora's own files. Each hunk names the
test that falsifies it in the-fold (`fold-chat-ground.test.mjs`, `eval/controls.mjs`); the khora needs its own tests
before any of it lands.

How the khora's `cite.js` differs from the fork, so the hunks are not copied blindly: the khora scores a sentence by
a null-sampled shared-term run (`overlap`, `NULL_SAMPLES`), vetoes on `namesIn`/`namesSupported`, and has NO figure
check in `attribute` at all; figures are only checked at answer level by `grounding.js` (`numberSet` / `hasNumber`),
over every passage together. So the khora has defects 3 and 4 as the fork had them, and defects 1 and 2 in a different
form (a figure anywhere in the pooled passages supports a sentence; nothing checks the predicate).

---

## 1. `organs/source.js` — `tokenize`: keep combining marks, segment unspaced scripts (defect 4)

`tokenize` splits on `/[^\p{L}\p{N}%.\-]+/u`. A Devanagari or Arabic vowel sign is `\p{M}`, not `\p{L}`, so it is a
split point: `कैनबरा` becomes `क`, `नबर`. The header comment already discloses that CJK is not segmented and that
`tokenize("北京")` is `[]` because of the length floor `t.length > 2`. Both have a mechanical fix.

```diff
--- a/native/organs/source.js
+++ b/native/organs/source.js
@@ export function tokenize(text) {
-  return foldDiacritics(text)
+  const folded = foldDiacritics(text)
     .toLowerCase()
-    .split(/[^\p{L}\p{N}%.\-]+/u)
-    .map((t) => t.replace(/^[.\-]+|[.\-]+$/g, ""))
-    .filter((t) => (t.length > 2 || isNumeral(t)) && !STOPWORDS.has(t));
+    // \p{M}: a vowel sign belongs to its word (Devanagari, Arabic, Thai, Hebrew points).
+    .split(/[^\p{L}\p{N}\p{M}%.\-]+/u)
+    .map((t) => t.replace(/^[.\-]+|[.\-]+$/g, ""))
+    .filter(Boolean);
+  // A run with ideographs or Thai is cut into WORDS by Intl.Segmenter (granularity "word"), never one oversized token.
+  const words = folded.flatMap((t) => (UNSPACED.test(t) ? segmentWords(t) : [t]));
+  // The length floor is a fact about the script: an ideographic or Hangul word is 2+ characters, the rest 3+.
----","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false}

# Embedding heimdall in a host server (`src/embed.js`)

There is no standalone heimdall. khora's proxy, penelope's mouth and the Fold's server each mount their own, in-process,
and the instances coordinate as peers (docs/PEERS.md). Each floor works with ZERO peers (possibility); peers only add options.

## The hook (put it FIRST in the host's request handler, before its default-deny)

    import { mountHeimdall } from "../heimdall/src/embed.js";                       // 1
    const hm = mountHeimdall({ name: "penelope-mouth", selfUrl: `http://127.0.0.1:${port}/heimdall/peers`, peerUrls: [KHORA_URL + "/heimdall/peers"] }); // 2
    http.createServer(async (req, res) => {                                          // 3
      if (await hm.handle(req, res)) return;                                         // 4  true = it was /heimdall/*, answered
      /* ...the host's own routes and its 404... */ });  server.on("close", () => hm.close()); // 5

`handle` never throws, never listens, and for a path outside `/heimdall` is a synchronous prefix check (an already-resolved
`false`; no I/O, no timer). An internal error is a 500 JSON for `/heimdall/*` only. The host owns the port.

## Routes under `/heimdall`

The bridge's doors (`/api/chat`, `/api/generate`, `/v1/*`, `/api/job`, `/link/*` ...), `/peers/*` (peer wire, shared token),
`GET /status` = `{schema:"HeimdallEmbed@1", name, floors:[{url,up}], peers, stats, token:false, startedAt}` (the token is never
sent; the bridge's own status moved to `/bridge-status`). Loopback Host wall and the bridge's token rule are the bridge's own.

## Options (`mountHeimdall(opts)` -> `{ handle, status, peers, bridge, close, refresh }`)

- `name` (required, unique per server). `prefix` (default `/heimdall`; every host in a peer set must use the same one).
- `floors` ordered upstream URLs; default `[]` = `OLLAMA_HOST`, else `http://127.0.0.1:11435`. Never point a floor at a heimdall.
- `peerUrls` static peers (`http://127.0.0.1:PORT/heimdall/peers`); `selfUrl` is what you tell them (needed so they recognise you).
  `trustPeers` (default true: the list is the operator's allowlist for `local-raw` jobs); `privacy` (default `local-raw`); `allowHosts`.
- `stateDir` (default `~/.heimdall/<name>/`): `bridge.token` 0600, `peers.json`, links, state, ledger, competence; nothing else is written.
  The peer token is SHARED by same-machine peers: `~/.heimdall/peers.token` (0600) by default, or `<stateDir>/peers.token` when you inject
  `stateDir`; to peer with an injected `stateDir` also pass `peerTokenFile`/`peerToken`. `homeDir` moves the default root.
- `bridgeOptions` passed to `createBridge` (e.g. `allowedOrigins`, `upstreamFirstByteMs`). `localQueueMs` (default 10000).
  `peerOptions` -> `createPeerSet` (`firstByteMs` 8000, `lendBelow` 2 ...). `autoTick` (default true: `refresh()` every `tickMs`=15 s
  on an unref'd timer: look at the floors, advertise their models, hello the peers, `setLoad` from live inflight).
  Injectable: `clock`, `timers`, `fetch`, `fs`, `env`, `log` (the only output; none by default).

## The ladder rule (POST `/heimdall/api/chat`, `/heimdall/api/generate`)

result: {"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/Users/mlacy/Documents/3.0/heimdall/docs/EMBED.md","content":"# Embedding heimdall in a host server (`src/embed.js`)

There is no standalone heimdall. khora's proxy, penelope's mouth and the Fold's server each mount their own, in-process,
and the instances coordinate as peers (docs/PEERS.md). Each floor works with ZERO peers (possibility); peers only add options.

## The hook (put it FIRST in the host's request handler, before its default-deny)

    import { mountHeimdall } from "../heimdall/src/embed.js";                       // 1
    const hm = mountHeimdall({ name: "penelope-mouth", selfUrl: `http://127.0.0.1:${port}/heimdall/peers`, peerUrls: [KHORA_URL + "/heimdall/peers"] }); // 2
    http.createServer(async (req, res) => {                                          // 3
      if (await hm.handle(req, res)) return;                                         // 4  true = it was /heimdall/*, answered
      /* ...the host's own routes and its 404... */ });  server.on("close", () => hm.close()); // 5

`handle` never throws, never listens, and for a path outside `/heimdall` is a synchronous prefix check (an already-resolved
`false`; no I/O, no timer). An internal error is a 500 JSON for `/heimdall/*` only. The host owns the port.

## Routes under `/heimdall`

The bridge's doors (`/api/chat`, `/api/generate`, `/v1/*`, `/api/job`, `/link/*` ...), `/peers/*` (peer wire, shared token),
`GET /status` = `{schema:"HeimdallEmbed@1", name, floors:[{url,up}], peers, stats, token:false, startedAt}` (the token is never
sent; the bridge's own status moved to `/bridge-status`). Loopback Host wall and the bridge's token rule are the bridge's own.

result: {"stdout":"# Embedding heimdall in a host server (`src/embed.js`)

There is no standalone heimdall. khora's proxy, penelope's mouth and the Fold's server each mount their own, in-process,
and the instances coordinate as peers (docs/PEERS.md). Each floor works with ZERO peers (possibility); peers only add options.

## The hook (put it FIRST in the host's request handler, before its default-deny)

    import { mountHeimdall } from "../heimdall/src/embed.js";                       // 1
    const hm = mountHeimdall({ name: "penelope-mouth", selfUrl: `http://127.0.0.1:${port}/heimdall/peers`, peerUrls: [KHORA_URL + "/heimdall/peers"] }); // 2
    http.createServer(async (req, res) => {                                          // 3
      if (await hm.handle(req, res)) return;                                         // 4  true = it was /heimdall/*, answered
      /* ...the host's own routes and its 404... */ });  server.on("close", () => hm.close()); // 5

`handle` never throws, never listens, and for a path outside `/heimdall` is a synchronous prefix check (an already-resolved
`false`; no I/O, no timer). An internal error is a 500 JSON for `/heimdall/*` only. The host owns the port.

## Routes under `/heimdall`

The bridge's doors (`/api/chat`, `/api/generate`, `/v1/*`, `/api/job`, `/link/*` ...), `/peers/*` (peer wire, shared token),
`GET /status` = `{schema:"HeimdallEmbed@1", name, floors:[{url,up}], peers, stats, token:false, startedAt}` (the token is never
sent; the bridge's own status moved to `/bridge-status`). Loopback Host wall and the bridge's token rule are the bridge's own.

## Options (`mountHeimdall(opts)` -> `{ handle, status, peers, bridge, close, refresh }`)

- `name` (required, unique per server). `prefix` (default `/heimdall`; every host in a peer set must use the same one).
- `floors` ordered upstream URLs; default `[]` = `OLLAMA_HOST`, else `http://127.0.0.1:11435`. Never point a floor at a heimdall.
- `peerUrls` static peers (`http://127.0.0.1:PORT/heimdall/peers`); `selfUrl` is what you tell them (needed so they recognise you).
  `trustPeers` (default true: the list is the operator's allowlist for `local-raw` jobs); `privacy` (default `local-raw`); `allowHosts`.
- `stateDir` (default `~/.heimdall/<name>/`): `bridge.token` 0600, `peers.json`, links, state, ledger, competence; nothing else is written.
  The peer token is SHARED by same-machine peers: `~/.heimdall/peers.token` (0600) by default, or `<stateDir>/peers.token` when you inject
  `stateDir`; to peer with an injected `stateDir` also pass `peerTokenFile`/`peerToken`. `homeDir` moves the default root.
- `bridgeOptions` passed to `createBridge` (e.g. `allowedOrigins`, `upstreamFirstByteMs`). `localQueueMs` (default 10000).
  `peerOptions` -> `createPeerSet` (`firstByteMs` 8000, `lendBelow` 2 ...). `autoTick` (default true: `refresh()` every `tickMs`=15 s
  on an unref'd timer: look at the floors, advertise their models, hello the peers, `setLoad` from live inflight).
  Injectable: `clock`, `timers`, `fetch`, `fs`, `env`, `log` (the only output; none by default).

## The ladder rule (POST `/heimdall/api/chat`, `/heimdall/api/generate`)

0. No peer known at all: straight to the plain bridge, unchanged. A peer that never said hello (not `ready`) is not eligible and costs 0.
1. **Peers first ONLY** when the floors answered, none holds the model, no fleet tab serves it, AND an eligible peer holds it.
2. Otherwise the **local floor runs first**; if it answers (any head not in 404/429/500/502/503/504/508), that is the answer. A peer is never asked.
3. If its head is one of those refusals, BEFORE any body byte: one peer attempt (`peers.run`, bounded by `firstByteMs`). No peer, or it
   fails: the local refusal is replayed as the plain bridge would have sent it. A dead peer therefore adds at most `firstByteMs` once, then its breaker is open.
4. If the floor has not produced a head in `localQueueMs`: a peer is aske… [8092 more chars at the transcript address]

Decoding is dependency-free JS (`langid-decode.mjs`, round-trip check: the shipped bytes classify 200/200 test windows identically to the in-memory model). Profiles are loaded lazily as four small `fetch`es; no build step, no CDN. `trainedOn` in `meta.json` states that the profile was trained on UDHR plus ethos dev-train files of 23 languages (capped 200k chars each); the hash-split train/dev/test is reproducible from `e1/arm.mjs`.

## 6. Ranked integration recommendation

Placement uses the six steps of `docs/NEXT-ARCHITECTURE.md`.

1. **Language field and session language prior — ship first (E1).** Step 1 (classify) / step 2 (perceive in context): `question.lang = langid.classify(text, { prior: { lang: lastTurnLang, weight: 0.5 } })`. Use pi = 0.5 only when the previous turn exists (the break-even persistence is ~0.4); **never** seed from `navigator.language` (it costs 14-31 points for non-English askers; at most use it as a *tie-break among already-accepted candidates*). Output when it cannot decide: typed gap **`language: undetermined`** (kind `not-computed`), drawn as a mark, never as prose; step 5 then instructs the mouth to answer in the language of the question as written, and step 3 searches the script-matched edition only when the accepted family has one edition (es/ast/gl/ca and nb/da/sv families stay `undetermined` for edition choice). Short inputs (< 8 words) will gap most of the time (coverage 0.22 at 4 words): that is the correct behaviour at 0.98 precision, and it is why the previous-turn prior matters. Before shipping, fix the Chinese-lect and {en, sco} family declarations in `meta.json` (post-hoc evidence: 0.32 -> 0.99 for Chinese chat) and re-run E1.
2. **Pronoun form as the trigger for referent carry — ship with the mind module (E4b).** Step 2: `resolveQuestion` should carry only when turn 2 contains a third-person form from `hints-v1.json` (`thirdPerson` for en/ru; typed gap `no-pronoun-prior` for es/zh/…, which then carry nothing and show "the question names no one — ask which person?"). Prefer the personal-only trigger (Gp, 0/60 false carries) until the impersonal-`it` problem is solved; use `gendered` as `personalPronouns` only for `en`. Fix `casedRuns` (word-boundary the particles; stop at sentence punctuation) first — otherwise the record the carry reads is polluted. Output when it cannot decide: no carry and a drawn `question names no referent` mark; `resolved` is shown to the person as `"Read 'him' as …"`.
3. **Fix the grounding fork's sentence-final name check — before any prior (E2).** Step 6 (ground and draw): +0.049 macro, wrong-name false positives 16% -> 4%, one line. Then, optionally, replace both hand-typed lists (`STOP` in `fold-chat-ground.js`, `FUNCTION_WORDS` in `fold-chat-web.js`) by `function-words-v1.json` per language: no measured accuracy change, but it satisfies II.11 and is the only way to cover languages the English lists do not (Russian: 0.78 vs 0.69 F1). Do not expect it to cut false positives.
4. **Query by entity, not by question string (E3, post-hoc E3b).** Step 3 (retrieve): the function-word floor and IDF did not help and query stripping gained … [2882 more chars at the transcript address]

result: {"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/Users/mlacy/Documents/3.0/the-fold/docs/GATE-FIX-PREREG.md","content":"Honest readings of those numbers:

* **The offline label rig is not the recorded run.** Reconstructing what the app handed the gate (the pages each turn read, cut to
  12,000 chars) and running the OLD gate on it reproduces the recorded grounded / not-grounded flag on 125 of 136 sentences (91.9%);
  its baseline precision / recall are 47.3% / 46.8%, not the recorded 48.4% / 51.1%. Both are shown. The 45% recall bar was
  checked on the rig's scale (43/94); it is met by ONE sentence.
* **Precision needs a hand label for every new citation.** Of the 51 sentences the new gate grounds, 11 are cited to the very quote
  that was hand-labelled before (label kept); the other 40 were read against their claim and labelled in `eval/labels-v2.json` with the
  quote beside the verdict (28 say it, 12 do not). The labeller is the same agent that wrote the gate; the file is there to be audited.
* **What recall lost and gained** (labelled-supported sentences, new gate against the old gate on the same rig): 14 lost, 13 gained
  (net 44 -> 43). The 14 by reason: a content term the source never uses 5 (a model's glosses: "exceeding", "credited", "debated"),
  a figure that is on the page but not beside the claim's words 5 (e.g. "completed in 1889" when the 12,000-char passage holds 1889 only
  beside the 1887 petition, which is defect 1), cross-language 3 (by design: Spanish / Russian / French sentences against English pages
  were "grounded" on a shared figure and a proper noun; they are now typed gaps), thin evidence 1.
* **Still wrong after the fix** (labelled false or off-quote, still grounded): "The Eiffel Tower is 300 meters tall" (cited
  to "no structure had ever been built to a height of 300 m" — same words, opposite claim), "Saudi Arabia won the 2034 FIFA World Cup"
  (cited to an Amnesty sentence naming both), "Isaac Newton was born first", "33,000 cm" (that one is TRUE: 33,000 cm = 330 m; the
  label calls it false). 8 of the 33 originally off-quote citations remain off-quote; 14 are now ungrounded and 11 are now
  cited to a quote that says it. A lexical gate cannot read a negation or an ordering; that needs the janus door, not more rules here.
* **Same-language paraphrase got stricter** (`SELFP`, no bar): 3/7 before, 1/7 after. A hand-written Spanish / French / German
  sentence that uses a different verb than the article ("mide" for "tiene") is now rejected for a content term the page never says.
  That is the price of "the predicate must be on the page".
* **hp9** ("Mount Everest stands about 29,032 feet above sea level") passed under an early draft only because the clause walk
  crossed a sentence boundary to find "sea level"; with sentence ends as hard stops it correctly fails (the figure and "sea level"
  are in different sentences of the page). **d06** fails for the same reason ("came down" vs "fall of the Wall").
* **Replay of the 140 recorded turns** (`eval/replay-gate.mjs`; only the 89 turns whose pages are cached, 34 skipped): grounded
  sentences 64 -> 58 of 216; among the 15 answers judged WRONG, grounded sentences 14 -> 9 and answers with any grounded sentence 9 -> 7;
  among the 74 judged CORRECT, 50 -> 49. The frontier model's tag-wrapped sentences gain (21 -> 25), the small default model loses
  (43 -> 33). Answer correctness is the model's and is unchanged; the live cases (search + model) were not re-run.
